axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It is "an entry point to a thousand-plus apps":
the user picks on the Zapier side which actions are exposed to the agent, and the server wraps those actions as MCP tools.
axes.runtime: Official hosted remote server (actions.zapier.com docs line direct fetch 200); each user gets a dedicated endpoint URL generated from their configuration.
axes.local_files: Never touches the local file system — what it executes on your behalf are Zapier-platform-side actions (reading and writing various SaaS apps).
axes.background:
The service lives on Zapier's side; request-response semantics. Note: Zapier's platform Zaps (the automation line) are resident automations —
that is another product surface in the automation category, not part of this MCP server itself.
axes.tools:
**A dynamic tool surface**: which tools are exposed = which actions of which apps the user checked in the Zapier MCP configuration
(Gmail/Sheets/Notion/Slack… a thousand-plus apps). The tool inventory varies per person and cannot be enumerated item by item —
this is its biggest structural difference from other vendor servers.
axes.context: No server-side cross-session memory — state lives in the various target apps.
axes.permissions:
**Two permission layers stack**: the Zapier-side "which actions are checked" is the first allowlist layer; each target app's
OAuth authorization is the second layer. Write capabilities follow the checkboxes — unchecked actions do not exist,
which is its structural tightening advantage over "single-app full-permission servers".
axes.fit:
Fits: one server reaching many apps (when an agent needs to touch Gmail+Sheets+CRM at once), tightening by action allowlist.
Not a fit: needing a deep single-app tool surface (official single-vendor servers go deeper); expecting free (Zapier plan-line constraints).

mcp.transport: **Streamable HTTP remote hosting** (a dedicated endpoint URL per user); verified: actions.zapier.com docs 200 (2026-10-21).
mcp.auth:
The endpoint URL itself carries authentication semantics (a dedicated secret endpoint) + OAuth for each target app;
endpoint leak = permission leak — treat its custody at credential grade.
mcp.scope:
Scope = the checked action set; both read and write (following each action's nature).
The allowlist is the first tightening layer; no official docs for a per-operation approval mechanism.
